sourceFlowReconstruction.L1-7: Mishnah: seven days before Yom Kippur the Kohen Gadol is separated from his house to the Parhedrin chamber; another kohen is prepared in his place lest a disqualification befall him. R. Yehuda: also another wife, lest his wife die, since 'vekhiper baado uvead beito', beito = his wife. They said to him: if so there is no end to the matter.
sourceFlowReconstruction.L8-14: Gemara cites 'tenan hatam': seven days before the burning of the parah the kohen who burns it is separated from his house to the chamber on the face of the Bira, northeast, called Lishkat Beit HaEven; why that name: all its acts are in dung, stone and earth vessels.
sourceFlowReconstruction.L14-20: Mai taama: since a tevul yom is fit for the parah (mishnah: they would make the burning kohen tamei and immerse him, to remove from the heart of the Sadducees who said it was done by those whose sun had set), the Rabbis instituted for it vessels that do not receive tumah so that it not be treated lightly.
L20-24 (s04): L20 'mai shna tzefonah mizrachah': anonymous Gemara asks what is different about (why) northeast - refers back to the cited mishnah's location of the chamber.
L20-21 'keivan dechatat hi': since it (fem. = the parah) is a chatat. Gemara only asserts it; Rashi: it is CALLED chatat, 'mei niddah chatat hi' (Num 19).

L21 'vechatat teunah tzefonah': and a chatat requires north. Rashi: chataot offered on the altar are slaughtered in the north; NOT that this one requires north, for it is slaughtered on Har HaMishchah.

L21-22 'ukhtiv bah el nokhach pnei ohel moed': and of it (bah = the parah) is written 'toward the front of the Tent of Meeting'. The Gemara does not say 'east'; Rashi: said of the sprinkling of its blood, he stands on Har HaMishchah, aims and sees the entrance of the Heikhal, which is in the eastern wall; Rashi later: 'teunah mizrach'.
L22-23 'takinu lah rabbanan lishkah tzefonah mizrachah': the Rabbis instituted for it (lah = the parah) a northeast chamber. Rabbinic enactment, no dispute, no named speaker.

L23-24 'ki heikhi delehavei lah hekeira': so that it have a distinguishing sign. Gemara does not say for whom/what; Rashi: to know that he was separated there in order to place on him the service of the parah, called chatat and requiring east, and he will set his heart to be zealous in its acts and the order of its services.
sourceFlowReconstruction.L24-27: Mai Bira: Rabba bar bar Chana in R. Yochanan's name: a place on the Temple Mount named Bira; Reish Lakish: the whole Temple is called Bira, 'habirah asher hakhinoti'.
sourceFlowReconstruction.L27-38: Mena hanei milei: R. Minyomi bar Chilkiya / R. Machseya bar Idi / R. Yochanan: 'kaasher asah bayom hazeh tzivah Hashem laasot lekhaper aleikhem' - laasot = acts of parah, lekhaper = acts of Yom Kippur. Whole verse cannot be parah (lekhaper; parah is not for atonement); perhaps whole verse is Yom Kippur? Gezerah shavah tzivah-tzivah with 'zot chukat hatorah'.
